claims.text: AlCrCuFeNi high-entropy-alloy thin films can be fabricated by electrodeposition.
Adjusting pulse energy and deposition time produces ultrananocrystalline AlCrCuFeNi films.
The electrodeposited AlCrCuFeNi films exhibit nanoscale phase separation.
The ultrananocrystalline films have a high density of grain boundaries and interfacial regions.
A high density of nanoscale grain boundaries enhances local electron scattering.
A high density of nanoscale grain boundaries alters local phonon modes or phonon spectra.
The grain-boundary-induced changes in scattering and phonon modes increase electron–phonon coupling.
The enhanced electron–phonon coupling promotes Cooper pairing.
Electron–phonon coupling governs the superconducting transition temperature in the proposed AlCrCuFeNi system.
The interfacial modification of electron–phonon coupling affects vortex dynamics.
Bulk-cast AlCrCuFeNi has a coarser conventional microstructure than the electrodeposited film.
Bulk-cast AlCrCuFeNi has fewer interfacial regions than the ultrananocrystalline film.
Ultrananocrystalline AlCrCuFeNi films will have a different, and potentially enhanced, superconducting transition temperature relative to bulk-cast AlCrCuFeNi.
Ultrananocrystalline AlCrCuFeNi films will exhibit vortex dynamics distinct from those of bulk-cast AlCrCuFeNi.
The proposed interfacial mechanism is dominant when grain size is below approximately 50 nm and interfacial density is high.
The proposed effect diminishes in a transitional grain-size regime or when other scattering mechanisms dominate.

contradictions.description: The samples are said to be synthesized under otherwise identical processing parameters, but the comparison changes both fabrication route and specimen form: electrodeposited thin films are compared with bulk-cast material. Those processing parameters cannot literally be identical, and route/thickness effects are therefore confounded with grain-boundary density.
